text:
maria: Hey support — customer org `org_842` reported they went to 0 credits in the middle of their billing cycle while running a long-lived streaming job + a batch embedding worker. They expect monthly refill at midnight but it never showed up for them. Any ideas?

support-joe: Which timezone do they report? Do we have the org's timezone or billing window?

maria: They are in PDT. Customer says UI showed 0 credits from ~2026-03-18T03:12:00Z and they kept getting 429s on streaming responses. Billing console shows "next refill: 2026-04-01T07:00:00Z" which seems wrong for their local midnight.

sam: @maria can you paste the org id and one request id from the 429s? Also did they hit any rate-limit headers (`x-rw-credits-remaining`, `x-rw-reset-ts`)?

maria: org_842, sample req id `req_8b3f2`. From their logs: `x-rw-credits-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-reset-ts: 1713744000` (they pasted the header exactly). They attach a screenshot of the UI showing 0 and a server-side metric of continuous small token drains.

support-joe: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) pro-rata logic for postpaid orgs aligned on UTC boundary but UI shows local midnight — that can look like delayed refill, 2) a background worker (embedding) retried in tight loop across the midnight boundary and burned the newly-refilled tokens before UI poll caught up.

liz: Also, we rolled a small fix last quarter for streaming reconnection accounting, but that was for double-counting chunk frames. This sounds like a different issue — maybe the refill happened but attribution went to a different project/tenant id?

sam: Repro steps I'd try: 1) check leaderboards for org_842 consumption by endpoint for 1 hour before/after their reported zero time, 2) grep payment/billing logs for actual refill event timestamp (server-side), 3) inspect any fast retries from worker IPs.

maria: I asked customer for the request id and a short HAR but they said it's internal. They can share one example websocket diag: `ws-frame id=... tokens_consumed=34` repeated every 3s. Could a keepalive or heartbeat be counted as content?

support-joe: Heartbeats shouldn't charge. But if their client is re-sending the last chunk on reconnect, that can reconsume tokens. Also check if they used both hosted and private endpoints that share the same monthly bucket — cross-service consumption is a common surprise.

sam: I'll pull the consumption breakouts now. If we see a refill event server-side before UI showed it, that means UI cache lag. If refill isn't present server-side, then it's a billing engine scheduling bug.

maria: Customer is on postpaid monthly billing with reserved capacity false. They emphasized this impacted production for ~27 minutes. They're asking for an expedited post-fix credit and a root cause note.

support-joe: Ok — contingency: offer to credit the gap for that 27min window while we investigate. Sam, can you confirm whether `1713744000` was a real reset ts from our ledger? If not, escalate to billing infra.

sam: Running ledger lookup now, will report back in 30m. tagging @billing-bot to capture any automation alerts.

billing-bot: Ledger lookup queued for org_842. ETA ~18 minutes. (automated) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: thanks — I'll tell the customer we are on it and offer temporary credits. I'll attach repro clues: long-lived stream + background embedder spikes at minute boundaries.

support-joe: Good. If anyone finds a quick patch (UI cache refresh or temporary top-up), do it and ping me. I'll draft the credit note once we confirm exact drained token count. :thumbsup:

(attachments: screenshot_of_ui.png, customer_ws_samples.log)
